nodes.summary: There are a nontrivial associative ring $R$ with identity, an integer $n \ge 3$ and a matrix $\sigma \in \mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ such that for all elementary transvections $\tau_1, \tau_2 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ the matrix $[[\sigma, \tau_1], \tau_2] - 1$ is not nilpotent, that is, $[[\sigma, \tau_1], \tau_2]$ is not unipotent. Here $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$, and an elementary transvection is a matrix $1 + r e_{ij}$…
nodes.title: Petechuk's double commutator question has a negative answer (Kourovka 10.46)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every nontrivial associative ring $R$ with identity, every $n \ge 3$ and every $\sigma \in \mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ there are elementary transvections $\tau_1, \tau_2 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ such that $[[\sigma, \tau_1], \tau_2]$ is unipotent, that is, $[[\sigma, \tau_1], \tau_2] - 1$ is a nilpotent matrix, where $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Petechuk's double commutator question (Kourovka 10.46)

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a matrix $\tau \in \mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ is an elementary transvection when $\tau = 1 + r e_{ij}$ for some indices $i \ne j$ and some nonzero $r \in R$, where $e_{ij}$ is the matrix unit with $1$ in position $(i, j)$ and $0$ elsewhere.
nodes.title: Elementary transvection
